items.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006
items.q: Then another time he said to me, “Don’t go home now, wait around I’ll take you for breakfast.” Okay, that was exciting, to go to breakfast with Duke.

ctx.x: Well let’s say Duke Ellington was very complex in the sense that he could adjust himself to whatever situation he was in. I did a party for Arthur Rice’s mother, who was going to

be 80 years old, I worked at the Rainbow Room and Duke Ellington was the artist that was performing with his orchestra. And I said to Mercer, who was part of his band and was very involved in his father’s career, that was Duke’s only son, “Merce, I got a lady that’s having a birthday party, 80 years, when the band breaks does their break let them all come for champagne and cake, it would make her very happy. She’ll be very excited.” And I invited everybody and they all came. And suddenly, who do I see come…
Why were his sidemen so mostly loyal to him?
